operator_console.a_box_s_role_is_just_th: A box's "role" is just the set of channels it runs. Self-asserted channels turn on with one click; governed channels are requested, then approved by the dual-meter.
operator_console.acts_under_a_peer_s_own: Acts under a peer's own zone — every co-affected peer must consent
operator_console.answerable_to_the_gover: Answerable to the government. Below a seated legislature the operator board (neutral + logged) relays rights-protection. The moment a legislature seats itself, the seated government supersedes the operator board — automatically, as a pure function of facts.
operator_console.each_open_proposal_show: Each open proposal shows its meters, kind by kind, on Versioning; role-grant approvals live on Roles.
operator_console.everything_on_this_cons: Everything on this console is also a command. These are the operator-plane verbs the console wraps.
operator_console.everything_raw_behind_o: Everything raw, behind one toggle. Closed by default.
operator_console.four_friendly_names_gro: Four friendly names group the capability channels — a role is just the set of channels it runs, and it adds no new power. Self-asserted roles turn on with one click; governed roles are requested, then approved by the dual-meter. Becoming a peer is one process for every node: get a certificate, take clients.
operator_console.governed_channels_need_: Governed channels need approval. Meter A runs the bootstrap path; the moment a legislature seats itself, Meter B supersedes it automatically. Meter C only attaches to channels that act under a peer's own zone.
operator_console.no_co_affected_peers_me: No co-affected peers — Meter C auto-passes.
operator_console.no_root_jurisdiction_ye: No root jurisdiction yet — the meters attach to a scope once the world is seeded.
operator_console.nothing_is_waiting_on_a: Nothing is waiting on a meter right now.
operator_console.off_the_constitutional_: Off the constitutional plane. Running a node is infrastructure, not a citizen privilege. It buys you no extra vote, no seat, no say in any constitutional act. Mesh state is a public record
operator_console.one_screen_for_the_box_: One screen for the box you run: are your peers reachable, is sync flowing, and which capabilities are live. The friendly view is the default — every channel slug and every meter lives one tap away under Advanced.
operator_console.signed_in_as_this_conso: Signed in as — this console is read-only; the role lifecycle actions live on the roles board.
operator_console.the_dot_is_the_rollup_e: The dot is the rollup: {rollupNote} Each chip is one of the readiness checks behind it — the same checks the command prints.
operator_console.the_full_tables_every_p: The full tables — every peer, the sync ledger, and the transport ladder — live in one place: Mesh & federation.
operator_console.the_mesh_console_is_sho: The mesh console is shown only to a signed-in operator. Operator accounts live on their own plane — they are not citizen users, and signing in here grants no citizen power.
operator_console.this_console_is_the_rea: This console is the read surface over the node's mesh services — the same gates the command prints, the same role and channel states the roles board acts on, and the same three consent meters that govern every capability grant and upgrade. Authority here always means a fact about a place — which node holds a jurisdiction's home copy — never a rank of node.
operator_home.a_box_s_role_is_just_the_s: A box's "role" is just the set of capability channels it runs — four friendly names group them. The full cards live on Roles & channels; turn them on from the console.
operator_home.each_line_says_what_to_do_: Each line says what to do next. A red gate blocks federation outright; an amber one just narrows what this box can offer.
operator_home.every_gate_passes_this_box: Every gate passes — this box can federate.
operator_home.full_faith_credit_one_reco: Full faith & credit — one record, many holders · Art. V
operator_home.lives_in_the_operations_co: Lives in the Operations console for now.
operator_home.none_yet_a_fresh_box_start: None yet — a fresh box starts quiet. Record Keeper is the recommended first turn-on: both of its channels are self-asserted.
operator_home.off_the_constitutional_pla: Off the constitutional plane. Running a node is infrastructure, not a citizen privilege — it buys you no extra vote, no seat, no say in any constitutional act. Operator vocabulary is "capability", never "role", so it can never collide with the citizen role system. Operators are an overlapping de-facto board, answerable to the in-game government — the moment a legislature seats itself, it supersedes the operator board automatically. Authority ≠ leadership.
operator_home.peers_sync_at_a_glance_tru: Peers & sync at a glance{peers} trusted of {peers2} peer{peers3} · last sync {lastSyncText} {label}
operator_home.run_a_node_and_your_comput: Run a node and your computer becomes part of the world — holding the record, naming peers, hosting the live rooms. This is the infrastructure the citizen game runs on, and it is deliberately separate from the constitutional game itself.
operator_home.the_capability_channels_th: The capability channels this box currently runs — a box's "role" is just this set. A governed channel went through the dual-meter consent; a self-asserted one is turned on by you alone.
operator_home.the_older_consoles_stay_re: The older consoles stay reachable while the campaign proves parity: Operations (legacy console) · Federation (legacy). Signed in as {operator}.
operator_home.the_operator_plane_s_front: The operator plane's front door: is this box ready to meet the mesh, which of the four named roles it runs, and one door to every operator surface. "Become a peer" is one process — a node that can get a certificate and take clients is a full, equal peer; role elevation is the separate, trust-gated ladder on Roles & channels.
operator_home.the_readiness_rollup_and_t: The readiness rollup and the mesh controls are shown only to a signed-in operator. You don't need anything here to play — the game lives on the civic pages.
operator_home.this_node_holds_the_home_c: This node holds the home copy of {homeCopies} place{homeCopies2}. Authority is a fact about where a place's home copy lives — never a rank of node: every peer holds the same record, and each place's home copy decides its writes.
operator_identity.a_device_enrols_its_ed: A device enrols its Ed25519 PUBLIC key — the secret never leaves the device (no escrow).
operator_identity.a_housekeeping_job_pru: A housekeeping job prunes lapsed attestations (already fail-closed on expiry; the sweep just bounds the table, soft-deleting for forensics).
operator_identity.a_person_on_a_journey_: A person on a journey can act through a server that isn’t their home, because their public standing travels as a signed, short-lived attestation. This attestation is what lets a visiting player act here.
operator_identity.a_short_lived_24h_revo: A short-lived (≤ 24h), revocable, instance-signed snapshot of a person’s derived standing, bound to a device key. Only the HOME authority attests. It carries only public standing — never credentials, locations, or ballots.
operator_identity.an_attestation_carries: An attestation carries only public standing. Role codes, the device key, the issuer, a TTL, and a signature — and nothing else. Never credentials, never locations, never ballots. Roles are still derived live, never stored.voting and candidacy are absolute rights, derived from residency, never persisted
operator_identity.each_device_enrols_its: Each device enrols its own key. Possession of a device key — never a password — is what other servers recognise.
operator_identity.enrolment_publishes_a_: Enrolment publishes a device’s public key; linking proves possession of an already-enrolled key on a new box. No secret ever leaves the device.
operator_identity.home_authority_attests: home authority attestsdevice signs the writenon-home engine verifies≤ 24h TTL · expiry sweep
operator_identity.mesh_operator_id_not_l: Mesh operator ID not linked to a mesh identity yet
operator_identity.no_devices_enrolled_ye: No devices enrolled yet. This operator account signs in with its local password only. Enrolling a device publishes its Ed25519 public key, so other boxes can recognise you by key possession.
operator_identity.only_the_home_authorit: Only the home authority attests · ≤ 24h · revocable · instance-signed
operator_identity.public_key_ed25519_the: Public key (Ed25519 — the public half only) not minted yet
operator_identity.standing_travels_the_r: standing travels; the right itself stays derived, never stored
operator_identity.subject_the_attested_u: Subject: the attested user resolves locally before authorization — citizenship is read live, never trusted from the wire alone.
operator_identity.the_ed25519_public_key: The Ed25519 public key is published; the secret half never leaves the device. There is nowhere for a private key to be escrowed.
operator_identity.the_enrolled_operator_: The enrolled operator device keys on this box
operator_identity.the_forwarded_write_is: The forwarded write is the keystone: a person passing through a server that isn’t home can still act, because their standing travels as a signed, short-lived attestation and their own device signs the action itself.
operator_identity.the_identity_layer_tha: The identity layer that lets a server know who you are across the mesh, and lets a citizen’s public standing travel with them onto a server that isn’t home. Two separate identities live here — yours as an operator, and the attested standing of a citizen passing through. They never touch.
operator_identity.the_identity_plane_is_: The identity plane is shown only to a signed-in operator. Nothing here carries constitutional power — it is how this box proves which box is talking.
operator_identity.the_plane_wall_holds_h: The plane wall holds here too. Operator identity is wholly separate from citizen identity — an operator account has no link to any citizen user.capability, not role
operator_identity.the_secret_half_of_the: The secret half of the signing key never leaves this box and never rides this page. Peers pin the public key; the node signs as itself.
operator_identity.this_box_has_not_cut_i: This box has not cut its Ed25519 signing keypair. It mints the first time federation needs it — reading this page never mints one.
operator_identity.two_identities_one_wal: Two identities, one wall. Your operator account proves which box is talking; a citizen’s attestation proves what they may do. Neither can be read as the other — and neither buys a constitutional privilege.off the constitutional plane
operator_identity.when_a_forwarded_write: When a forwarded write arrives, it must clear all three checks before the engine will authorize it. Any failure is fail-closed.
operator_identity.who_this_box_is_on_the: Who this box is on the mesh, and who you are on this box. This is infrastructure identity — it grants no vote, no seat, no constitutional say.
operator_identity.your_local_password_si: Your local password signs you in on this box only — other boxes recognise you by device-key possession, never by a password.
operator_mesh.every_box_this_node_has_ha: Every box this node has handshaked with, and where each one sits in the trust lifecycle. The relation chip records how you stand to each peer — it describes data placement, never a rank.
operator_mesh.federation_url_how_peers_a: Federation URL — how peers address this box:
operator_mesh.for_every_jurisdiction_one: For every jurisdiction, one box's record is the authoritative one — a bookkeeping fact about where the home copy lives, never a rank. A player can act on any node: the action is verified — signed by their own device, carrying an attestation from their home server — and forwarded to the place's home copy.
operator_mesh.full_faith_credit_the_sync: Full Faith & Credit — the sync ledger
operator_mesh.how_your_node_finds_its_pe: How your node finds its peers, carries their records, and survives a hostile network — the federation layer the citizen game rides on.
operator_mesh.no_peers_yet_this_box_stan: No peers yet — this box stands alone. Joining a cluster starts with a one-shot join-key minted by a host operator; the join wizard runs on the operations (legacy) console this campaign. Joining never moves authority: which box holds a place's home copy stays exactly where it was.
operator_mesh.no_sync_entries_yet_the_le: No sync entries yet — the ledger starts writing the moment a peer carries records to or from this box.
operator_mesh.no_transports_advertised_y: No transports advertised yet — peers can still reach this box at its federation URL below, but registering transports gives the mesh fallback rungs when that URL fails.
operator_mesh.nothing_is_lost_and_nothin: Nothing is lost and nothing pauses: reads continue everywhere throughout, and forwarded writes queue until the flip lands.
operator_mesh.off_the_constitutional_pla: Off the constitutional plane. Joining, syncing and naming peers are capabilities — they buy no vote, no seat, and no say in any constitutional act.
operator_mesh.one_process_to_peerage_aut: One process to peerage — authority attaches to a place, never a node
operator_mesh.only_two_things_services_a: Only two things. Services a box's hardware can't host — a small box might skip voice or the live rooms. And the trust-gated naming channels, which reach under other peers' zones and so need those peers' consent.
operator_mesh.peers_transports_and_the_s: Peers, transports and the sync ledger are shown only to a signed-in operator of this box. Citizens play the game; operators keep the box on the mesh.
operator_mesh.re_peer_every_other_node_r: Re-peer — every other node re-points at the new home copy on its next sync.
operator_mesh.sealed_export_the_departin: Sealed export — the departing box seals a signed export of the jurisdiction's records.
operator_mesh.the_same_signed_bytes_ride: The same signed bytes ride any advertised channel, tried in priority order — so the mesh survives even when the open internet does not. These are the endpoints this box advertises to its peers.
operator_mesh.the_sync_ledger_is_append_: The sync ledger is append-only and public — like every record on the constitutional plane, it can be read by anyone and never rewritten.
operator_mesh.there_is_one_path_to_peera: There is one path to peerage, and every node walks it: get a certificate, take clients, and hold the whole public record. Once you're in, your box is a full, equal peer — it serves players like any other node. Role elevation is the separate, trust-gated ladder on Roles & channels.
operator_mesh.this_console_reads_the_mes: This console reads the mesh as it is — peers from the handshake registry, our advertised transports, the live peerage gates, and the last 25 entries of the append-only sync ledger. Every join, sync and departure it shows was recorded by the federation services; the page changes nothing. Cluster join is infrastructure, not a constitutional act: it grants no vote, no seat, and no authority over any place's record.
operator_mesh.trust_lifecycle_discovered: Trust lifecycle: discovered · handshake · trust established · syncing · border settled
operator_mesh.verified_flip_the_receivin: Verified flip — the receiving peer verifies it against the audit chain, and the mesh records the new home.
operator_mesh.what_this_box_still_needs_: What this box still needs before (or to remain) a full peer — a certificate, an identity, a reachable URL. Each gate is probed live; nothing here is a rank, only readiness.
operator_mesh.when_a_home_box_retires_or: When a home box retires (or its government chooses a new host), authority moves in three verified steps:
operator_mesh.when_peers_carry_one_anoth: When peers carry one another's records, the sync ledger is the receipt. Each row is one push or pull, with its result and the record range it covered. An “authority disputed → resolved” result means the dispute resolved in favour of the place's home copy — the constitutional record never forks.
operator_operations.instant_tier_knobs_a: Instant-tier knobs are edited in place (applied on the next request). Restart-tier LiveKit networking is applied via the host supervisor above. Secret rotation is intentionally not yet wired — it is gated on the credential-security pass; rotate via matrix:setup for now.
operator_operations.no_dns_credential_st: No DNS credential stored. Set one (write-only) on the Federation console.
operator_operations.none_installed_under: None installed under the TLS path.
operator_operations.signed_in_as_secrets: Signed in as {operator}. Secrets show only whether they are set — values never leave the box.
operator_operations.the_infrastructure_i: The infrastructure & identity plane for this box — certificates, DNS, voice, and Matrix. Separate from the constitution: the operator manages the box, the constitution governs the polity. This view is read-only; the documentation links explain how to change each knob today.
operator_operations.the_operations_inven: The operations inventory is shown only to a signed-in operator.
operator_operations.these_knobs_are_env_: These knobs are env-baked, so applying rewrites .env and recreates the container — which the app can't do from inside itself. A host-side supervisor does it: run python3 scripts/ops/infra_supervisor.py on the host first (see the LiveKit runbook). No secrets are applyable here.
operator_operations.waiting_for_the_host: {applyLabel} — waiting for the host supervisor. Is scripts/ops/infra_supervisor.py running on the host? — {error}
operator_roles.a_box_s_role_is_nothing_m: A box’s “role” is nothing more than the set of capability channels it runs. Trust here is composable — you add the channels you can serve, one at a time. There are no tiers to climb and no rank to earn.
operator_roles.a_governed_channel_is_app: A governed channel is approved by a dual-meter — operators while no government is seated, the seated government the moment one exists — plus a third meter for the few channels that reach under a peer’s zone. The meters below are live reads; nothing here re-counts a vote.
operator_roles.a_governed_channel_walks_: A governed channel walks four plain steps. A self-asserted channel skips straight to Active — there is no request and no approval to wait on.
operator_roles.a_seated_government_appro: A seated government approves through its own vote — this button can only attest Meter A, and the grant will refuse with its citation until that vote passes.
operator_roles.approval_mints_a_verified: Approval mints a verified grant — dual-meter consent (Art. VII admissibility; seated-government supersession), never a self-claim. Dropping one of your own channels is always unilateral.
operator_roles.four_friendly_names_group: Four friendly names group the nine channels — no new power, just a grouping. Each card shows its channel set, the duty you take on, and whether it turns on by itself or needs a government decision.
operator_roles.leave_blank_for_the_root_: Leave blank for the root jurisdiction. A grant acts over a place — never over the mesh as a rank.
operator_roles.no_open_role_grant_reques: No open role-grant requests. A governed request you or a peer opens will appear here with its live meter state.
operator_roles.off_the_constitutional_pl: Off the constitutional plane. Running a node is infrastructure, not a citizen privilege — it buys you no extra vote, no seat, no say in any constitutional act. Operator accounts have no link to citizen users. Signed in as {operator} · a grant always attaches to a place{scope} — never to a node as a rank.
operator_roles.open_role_grant_requests_: Open role-grant requests with live consent-meter reads
operator_roles.qualify_probes_whether_th: Qualify probes whether this box can host the channel — it changes nothing. Request turns a self-asserted channel on, or opens a governed request for the dual-meter to decide.
operator_roles.read_write_authority_is_a: Read–write authority is a fact about a place — where its home copy lives. It moves between consenting nodes per jurisdiction; it is not a rank this box petitions for.
operator_roles.self_a_self_asserted_chan: self a self-asserted channel · governed a governed channel
operator_roles.self_asserted_mesh_member: Self-asserted (mesh.member · mirror · etl): establishActive — one click, no gate.
operator_roles.self_asserted_vs_governed: Self-asserted vs governed. A self-asserted channel touches nobody but you, so it is yours to switch on. A governed channel either grants a duty over other people or writes a name under a peer’s zone — so it is requested, never claimed, and approved by the dual-meter below.
operator_roles.the_nine_capability_chann: The nine capability channels, their consent kind, live state on this node, and actions
operator_roles.the_roles_board_is_shown_: The roles board is shown only to a signed-in operator. Operator accounts live on the operator plane — they have no link to citizen users and carry no citizen power.
operator_roles.the_whole_closed_vocabula: The whole closed vocabulary. Three channels are self-asserted — mesh.member, mirror, and etl — and need no gate at all: they only ever describe what your own box does. The other six are governed, because each one grants a duty over others, or hangs a name under a peer’s zone.
operator_roles.this_channel_acts_under_a: This channel acts under a peer’s zone — co-affected peers must also consent (Meter C).
operator_roles.waiting_on_the_dual_meter: Waiting on the dual-meter — see the pending list below.
operator_roles.you_are_the_founding_oper: You are the founding operator. There is no mesh to answer to and no government seated yet, so every role is yours to switch on directly — governed channels included. Once your world is founded and a government seats, governed channels return to the dual-meter consent path for any later change.
operator_versioning.a_and_b_are_two_legs: A and B are two legs of one seat — the operator board attests only while no government is seated; the moment one seats, its supermajority supersedes the board. C is every trust-established peer holding the home copy of a co-affected place (unanimous; it passes on its own when no such peer exists).
operator_versioning.a_divergent_version_: A divergent version stops the sync rather than silently merging mismatched rules. The other side agrees the upgrade — through the same meters below — before its tail flows again.
operator_versioning.a_proposal_is_screen: A proposal is screened first, agreed second. Each meter that applies must pass; a meter that doesn't apply to the proposal's kind or scope simply isn't needed.
operator_versioning.a_running_election_o: A running election or session pins its version.
operator_versioning.answerable_to_the_go: Answerable to the government. Operators run the upgrade; they never author the rule. The filter is hardened, the freeze is mechanical, and the seated government has the final say.
operator_versioning.derived_from_the_rul: derived from the rules in force
operator_versioning.every_peer_advertise: Every peer advertises its constitutional version. A peer on a different version cannot be synced into — the mesh refuses fail-closed until both sides have agreed an upgrade.
operator_versioning.every_proposal_passe: Every proposal passes the hardened admissibility filter before any consent is counted. One that would lower proportionality, or drop the supermajority floor below majority-plus-one, is refused outright — no meter, no operator, and no amount of reach can wave it through.
operator_versioning.how_a_version_change: How a version changes hands across the mesh — what this node runs, what every peer advertises, and the open proposals waiting on consent. Every constitutional change is screened by the hardened filter first, then agreed by the people who actually hold the power.
operator_versioning.no_meters_this_kind_: no meters — this kind moves mechanically
operator_versioning.no_open_proposals_th: No open proposals — the mesh agrees on the version in force.
operator_versioning.no_peers_yet_this_bo: No peers yet — this box stands alone. Versions start to matter the moment a second box joins the mesh.
operator_versioning.off_the_constitution: Off the constitutional plane. Upgrading the software is an operator-plane capability, not a citizen privilege. The constitutional rules themselves are never edited from here — a version change is proposed, screened, and only then agreed by the people who actually hold the power.
operator_versioning.peer_constitutional_: Peer constitutional versions and app releases
operator_versioning.pinning_is_a_pure_fu: Pinning is a pure function of the contest record; there is no manual override to thaw a running game.
operator_versioning.proposed_by_node_for: proposed by node {shortId} · for the place {shortId2} · consent falls to {legLabel}
operator_versioning.the_constitutional_v: the constitutional version — a fingerprint of the hardened rules in force
operator_versioning.this_console_renders: This console renders the versioning truth held by the upgrade-agreement service — it never re-implements a meter or moves a version itself. Proposals are driven through the mesh services; a regressive constitutional bump can never pass the hardened filter, no matter who consents.
operator_versioning.three_kinds_of_versi: Three kinds of version move independently. Only the constitutional one touches the hardened surface — it alone passes the filter and the meters below; app releases and schema bumps move mechanically.
operator_versioning.versions_and_upgrade: Versions and upgrade proposals are shown only to a signed-in operator. Nothing is decided here without consent — a version change clears the meters, never a console.
operator_versioning.when_play_begins_the: When play begins, the contest captures the constitutional version in force at that moment. Any agreed upgrade lands for the next contest — never the one mid-play — so no one can change the rules under the ballots already cast.
